title: Minimal Polynomial Reduction and Annihilator Theory

problemStatement.formal: For any polynomial f and matrix M over a field K: aeval M f = aeval M (f %ₘ minpoly K M), with deg(f %ₘ minpoly K M) < deg(minpoly K M) ≤ n
problemStatement.plain: The minimal polynomial provides the tightest polynomial reduction for matrix evaluation, strictly refining the characteristic polynomial reduction.
whyMatters: The minimal polynomial generates the annihilator ideal of a matrix, characterizing all polynomial relations
Reduction via minpoly gives potentially smaller degree than charpoly (for derogatory matrices)
Connects to Jordan form theory: minpoly encodes sizes of largest Jordan blocks
Essential in control theory: observability/controllability depend on minpoly = charpoly

proven: Minimal polynomial reduction: aeval M f = aeval M (f %ₘ minpoly K M)
Degree bounds: reduced polynomial has degree < deg(minpoly) ≤ n
Annihilator ideal characterization: aeval M f = 0 ↔ minpoly K M ∣ f
Annihilator ideal closure under addition and multiplication
Congruence modulo minpoly: same remainder implies same matrix evaluation
Equivalence: aeval M f = aeval M g ↔ minpoly K M ∣ (f - g)
Power reduction: M^k = aeval M (X^k %ₘ minpoly K M)
Every evaluation reducible to polynomial of degree < deg(minpoly)
Comparison: charpoly reduction refines to minpoly reduction
Minpoly degree bounds: 0 < deg(minpoly) ≤ deg(charpoly) = n
Nonzero annihilating polynomial has degree ≥ deg(minpoly)
Nilpotent from minpoly: minpoly M = X^d implies M^d = 0
Higher nilpotent powers vanish: M^k = 0 for k ≥ d
Idempotent: M^2 = M implies minpoly M ∣ X^2 - X
Involutory: M^2 = I implies minpoly M ∣ X^2 - 1
Identity annihilated by X - 1, zero matrix annihilated by X

Proves the minimal polynomial reduction theorem, annihilator ideal characterization, degree bounds, congruence theory, power reduction, and comparison with characteristic polynomial reduction. Also covers special matrix classes: nilpotent, idempotent, involutory, scalar, identity, and zero matrices.
builtItems: aeval_eq_aeval_mod_minpoly: core minimal polynomial reduction theorem
insights: Minimal polynomial reduction is strictly tighter than charpoly reduction for derogatory matrices
Annihilator ideal is principal, generated by minpoly (K[X] is a PID over fields)
Two polynomial expressions equal iff their difference is divisible by minpoly
Every polynomial expression in M reduces to degree < deg(minpoly), which can be < n
Charpoly reduction can always be further refined by minpoly reduction
For scalar matrix cI: minpoly has degree 1 while charpoly has degree n

approaches.name: Direct proof via polynomial division and Mathlib API
approaches.description: Uses Polynomial.modByMonic_add_div for division algorithm, minpoly.aeval for annihilation, minpoly.dvd for universal property. All results proved directly from Mathlib's minpoly and charpoly infrastructure.
